newsitem.title: USA: Use natural ways to curb pests-U.S. consumer group.
newsitem.headline: Use natural ways to curb pests-U.S. consumer group.

text.p: A U.S. consumer group Tuesday called for less chemical pesticides and more so-called natural techniques to control pests and diseases that attack plants and animals.
In a 288-page report, Consumers Union advocated "integrated pest management (IPM)," which uses natural predators or times crops to minimize pest damage.
The group favored biointensive IPM which would allow the use of reduced-risk pesticides only if other tactics fail.

"We're on a 'pesticide treadmill,'" said Charles Benbrook, lead researcher for the report. "Not only don't chemical methods of pest control work as well as they should, they pose substantial ecological and economic risks."
Consumers Union suggested the doubling of crop acreage under biointensive IPM by the end of the decade. All U.S. crop acreage would come under biointensive IPM by 2020 under the group's proposal.

To encourage the shift, it said businesses should buy from IPM farms and more federal research funds should be made available. It said "effective IPM strategies now exist for many pest problems" but acknowledged an experienced hand is usually needed.
